audience: Owners and principals of established Sydney strata and property management firms
problem: A repair, renovation or supplier approval lives across forwarded emails, so the manager becomes the only person who can reconstruct its status.
single_message: Give every approval one visible record, decision owner, deadline and exception path while keeping authority and judgement human.
supporting_points: Tie the request to the correct scheme, documents, authority and deadline
Move routine reminders and status updates without turning email into a second source of truth
Write the recorded decision back to the work order and requester
Keep disputed scope, urgent safety, conflicts and committee judgement with people
desired_action: Book an on-site automation review and trace one real approval from request to outcome
angle: The expensive problem is not the approval itself. It is the manager repeatedly reconstructing a decision that has no visible owner or status.

visual_concept: A realistic modern Sydney strata lobby where one ochre approval folder is visibly stuck in an otherwise orderly document system.

article_outline: The expensive moment is the status chase
Create one approval record, not another inbox rule
Connect the trigger to the next commercial step
Keep authority, risk and judgement human
Measure recovered capacity, not email volume
Start with one approval that keeps coming back
search_question: How do strata managers stop approval requests disappearing into email?
direct_answer: Strata managers stop approvals disappearing by giving every request one visible record with the scheme, documents, decision owner, deadline, status and exception path, while leaving authority and judgement with the right people.
promotion_hypothesis: The visible cost of approval chasing should resonate with established strata principals, but paid use remains a hypothesis until qualified outcomes exist.
